A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the combination of s imeprevir and T MC647055/rit onavir, with or without rib avirin, is associated with a low virologic failure rate and a low rate of emergence of resistance-associated variants ( RAVs) in chronic HCV genotype  1-infected patients, including patients with cirrhosis and patients with prior null responses to pegylated interferon and ribavirin (PegIFN/RBV).
the combination of SMV and TCM647055/RT was well tolerated in HCV genotype-1 patients, with a high SVR12 rate.

we have identified and characterised pre-existing and emerging RAVs in patients enrolled in a phase 2 study with the 3-D AA regimen SMV ± RBV, TMC647055 and JNJ-56814845, and in patients who received the 2-D AA regimen SM + RBV, and TMC64755.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of s imeprevir, TMC647055 and JNJ- 56914845 was highly active against genotype 1a HCV.
the emergence of RSVs to all study DAA drugs is associated with virologic breakthrough in this study.
the combination of SMV and TCM647055/RT is not effective in HCV genotype-1 infected patients.
